stories.repeat_check: Nvidia posted often (11-07 naver, 11-09 rebellions); earnings and China exit not covered in last 14 days. Huang scandal items carry brand-safety risk (affairs, SEC): lead on numbers and China, omit personal allegations.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang's ouster
Nvidia's startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang's exit puts future deals in doubt

facts.text: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue (quarter ended October 25, 2026) of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago.
Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago.
Nvidia's outlook for the fourth quarter is revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, and it is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China.
Nvidia said it has shipped Vera Rubin NVL72, the fastest product ramp in the company's history.
Colette Kress is interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of Nvidia.

Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company's participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

Jefferies forecast that the new U.S. rules, which bar advanced chips from foreign data centers serving Chinese customers remotely, might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia's data center revenue next year; Kress said the backlog of demand means the rules would have no impact on top-line revenue.
Nvidia's equity stakes in private companies are now worth $65.5 billion, up from $22 billion reported in January; it invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: #2 on Artificial Analysis index, API price cut 20%
stories.repeat_check: No GPT-6.2 post in 14 days (11-06 gpt6-cyber was a different story). Original OpenAI page blocked (403); source is AI Times (Korean) quoting OpenAI blog and Artificial Analysis. Better as evening-slot style US story.

articles.title: 오픈AI, 세계 2위 성능 'GPT-6.2 아스트라' 출시...API 20% 인하

facts.text: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17 (US time), about 50 days after cancelling the GPT-6.1 Astra release over safety problems.
On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, GPT-6.2 Astra scored 62, second behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 (65), ahead of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon (60) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59).
GPT-6.2 Sol scored 57 and reached a similar overall level to GPT-6 Astra at about 15% of the cost per task.
GPT-6.2 Astra API price is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, 20% lower than before; cached input fell from $1.00 to $0.40.
GPT-6.2 Sol is priced at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, unchanged.
OpenAI said GPT-6.2 Astra is the first publicly released model to reach the High level in its AI Self-improvement risk category, and both models are rated Critical in cybersecurity capability.
On Artificial Analysis's coding agent index, Astra stayed level with the previous version and Sol fell 3 points.
The models are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and via API; not yet in regular ChatGPT chat.

stories.repeat_check: No Moonshot post in 14 days. Two sources (heise, AI Times); both cite SCMP, which was not read directly.

articles.title: Moonshot AI wechselt Entwicklungsfokus von Programmierung zu Wissenschaft
[11월17일] 미국 이어 중국도 'AI 과학적 발견' 경쟁…문샷, 생물학·화학 연구에 집중

facts.text: Moonshot AI, the company behind the Kimi models, wants to push into scientific applications of AI; the head of its international business said so in a keynote at Web Summit in Lisbon (heise, quoting SCMP).
He said coding has reached a plateau, and that science raises the intelligence level further.
"We focus strongly on biology and chemistry," he said, while OpenAI is focused on mathematics.
DP Technology, a Beijing AI-for-science startup, said it will use Kimi K3.1 Pro for biological research tasks.

In a demo, DP Technology's BioMaster agent with Kimi analysed gene expression data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and identified 100 candidate genes in about 90 minutes, more than twice as fast as a human.

Moonshot's TCSExam study, published on the 5th by founder Yang Zhilin and Turing Award winner Andrew Yao, tested models on 100 research tasks; US frontier models led overall and no model solved a long-standing open problem independently.
AI Times notes the Kimi result automates data analysis and candidate search and is not proof of a new scientific discovery.

stories.title: Tencent Hy4 Flash: up to 95% lower cost per task, API $0.07 per million input tokens
stories.repeat_check: PARTIAL REPEAT: 2026-11-05-tencent-hy4 covered the larger Hy4. Different model, but same company within 14 days; second Chinese model after Qwen4-Max (11-17).

facts.text: Tencent released Hy4 Flash on November 16 (local time), a low-cost model for everyday work such as documents, presentations and research.
In Tencent's own evaluation it cuts cost per task by up to 95% versus earlier models while user satisfaction came close to Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5.
It is a mixture-of-experts model with 224 billion total parameters and 12 billion active per token, supports images and up to 1 million tokens of context.
API price is $0.07 per million input tokens and $0.281 per million output tokens; cached input is $0.003.
On Tencent's WorkIndex, cost per task is one thirteenth of Hy4 Preview, one twentieth of Hy4 and one eighth of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
In a blind test with 85 Tencent employees across 259 tasks using the WorkBuddy agent, it had the lowest cost per task and shortest completion time among compared models.
Tencent plans to release the model weights later; results are Tencent's own evaluations.

stories.title: AI-made ballad 'The Adult I Dreamed Of' tops Korea's Melon chart
stories.repeat_check: No repeat (11-08 suno-elvis-eminem is a different story). Nikkei Asia also ran it 11-16 (link redirect not read). Reference accounts: none.

facts.text: The ballad "The Adult I Dreamed Of" ranked No. 1 on Melon's Top 100 for three consecutive days as of Sunday, becoming the first song composed and sung entirely by AI to top the chart (per the outlet; other outlets call it AI-assisted).
Melon is one of Korea's major music streaming platforms.

The song is by AI musician Meomuru, behind which are composers and producers Lee Yong-seok and Choi Seong-hyeok, who wrote the lyrics and shaped the direction, then used AI to create the arrangement, melody and vocals.
It held No. 1 against A2O Lite's "Neon" (2nd), Rescene's "With" (3rd) and ILLIT's "You're Under Arrest" (4th).
It first topped YouTube's daily trending music video chart on Sept. 2, reached No. 29 on Melon by Oct. 2 and the top three on Oct. 15.
Its popularity grew as people used it as background music for Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.

The duo has reportedly been unable to collect royalties because the track is not registered with the Korea Music Copyright Association; under current rules all AI-generated songs are ineligible for copyright registration.
In August the association announced criteria recognizing human contributions to AI-assisted music but later withdrew them over insufficient public consultation.

articles.title: Five firms team up to bid for a Nordic-Baltic AI gigafactory

facts.text: Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda formed a group, AI Gigafactory Northern, to bid for one of the EU's planned AI gigafactories, spread across several Nordic and Baltic sites.
Sites named so far are Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia and Valmiera in Latvia; a fourth site in Sweden has no location yet.
The bid goes to a tender run by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, which also runs Europe's shared supercomputers such as Finland's LUMI.
Each gigafactory must hold three to four times as many top AI processors as Europe's most powerful AI factories.
The second lot's deadline is 3 December; on 5 November the first lot's deadline moved to 4 February 2027.
The release ties the plan to InvestAI, through which the EU aims to raise EUR30bn for AI: EUR20bn private and EUR10bn public money.
Nokia supplies the network; Nscale and Finland's Verda bring platforms for training and running models; Telia adds connectivity and cloud; Estonia's Skeleton Technologies makes power systems.
VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and Sweden's KTH Royal Institute of Technology back the group.

articles.title: AI cheating scandal sparks fears before college exam

facts.text: A candidate identified only as H, who topped Korea's certified tax accountant examination in April, confessed to cheating with a miniature camera and generative AI.
The college entrance exam (CSAT) is on Thursday; about 550,000 students will take it simultaneously at 1,312 testing centers.
Late last month the Ministry of Education banned all electronic devices, including AI glasses, smartphones and smartwatches, from exam rooms.
Offenders would have scores invalidated, lose eligibility the following year and potentially face criminal obstruction charges.
The editorial says miniature cameras are almost impossible to identify by visual inspection and notes China uses checkpoints, metal detectors and wireless-signal blocking.

articles.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO

facts.text: Anthropic disclosed that Amazon's total stake will come in at 14.7% after the IPO.
If Amazon converted all its promissory notes now it would own 23.8%; conversion prices are about $2.09 or $5.05 per share.
Google will own just under 14% (13.7%), in non-voting shares.
AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to buy $26 billion worth of non-voting stock; Google and Nvidia each $10 billion.
Anthropic is committed to spend more than $100 billion on AWS over the next decade.

articles.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases

facts.text: Tasks is a toggle in Gemini that turns the chatbot into a more active helper.
Google says it can call businesses and book appointments for users, complete purchases via Google Pay, and sign into websites securely if prompted.
It launched to select testers in May as Gemini Spark, then went to US Google AI Ultra subscribers.
Google is now making it free to hundreds of millions of people using the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
